items.title: Susan's chopping down her giant tree while she still can, ahead of rule change

children.content: A home owner in Perth’s south plans to cut down a “beast” of a tree, a 20-metre-tall Norfolk Pine, in order to beat the introduction of the council's policy to protect large trees amid a dwindling tree canopy.

children.content: Small businesses are being hit with "underpaid postage fees", but Australia Post says its size and weight scanners are "highly accurate" and will not disclose how often its technology is wrong, raising questions about the legality of its additional charges.

items.title: Winners and losers of Labor's $560m community grants

children.content: Some seats were offered tens of millions of dollars in funding for sports clubs, parks and more, while 45 seats were given nothing out of an "invite-only" grant program now under scrutiny over pork barrelling claims.

items.title: Perth man once charged over backpacker's murder breaks silence after 20 years

children.content: More than two decades after he last spoke publicly, Tobias Moran tells the ABC he did not kill his girlfriend Simone Strobel in Lismore in 2005 and accuses the police of unfairly targeting him.

items.title: Women's tennis has a new world number one as US Open showdown looms

items.title: Oldest known evidence of human drug use discovered in fossil teeth

image.altText: Fragments of a skull with a jagged jawline against a black background.

items.title: Prosecutors say man asked ChatGPT for legal help after alleged data breach

children.content: A Sydney man charged over a massive data breach involving a NSW courts website allegedly used generative AI to create "scraper" computer code for bulk downloading before asking ChatGPT for legal advice, a court hears.

image.altText: A young man in a white shirt and jeans, with a scarf covering part of his face, walking outside a court building.

items.title: Opals survive in last second after giving up 20-point lead at World Cup

children.content: A short-handed Australian team is still alive and into the quarterfinals at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup despite surrendering a 20-point three-quarter-time lead against Italy.

image.altText: Isobel Borlase and Opals teammates put their hands on their heads in shock at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.
